Question Choices: For a nonconstant degree-n polynomial with complex coefficients, how many complex roots does the fundamental theorem of algebra guarantee, counting multiplicity?
Hints: The degree controls the total root count.|Repeated roots count repeatedly.
Solution: The fundamental theorem of algebra says a nonconstant degree-n polynomial with complex coefficients has exactly n complex roots counting multiplicity. Real roots are included among complex roots. Repeated roots need not be distinct; the leading coefficient multiplies the complete linear factorization. It has exactly n complex roots counting multiplicity.
